label: Objective adequacy: whatever causes an idea's representing r has r, IN_ACT_4
paraphrase: P3 of the idea-of-the-infinite argument, analyst formulation of objective adequacy (navigation: Descartes, Meditation III and the Second Replies axiom on objective reality; attribution deferred): whatever is a cause of an idea e's representing a perfection r is itself in act in r, formally or eminently (IN_ACT_4, mode of possession left open). A separate premise, not an instance of the formal containment clause (634a80b8): the separation control 'Formal containment does not give objective adequacy' shows that formal containment and q.4 a.2 preexistence allow the cause of an idea of r to have only the feature of representing r. Partial causes of the objective reality are included. Open.
